content.text: Kinetics asks how rapidly a system changes, not merely whether one equilibrium state has lower Gibbs energy. Reaction rates depend on mechanism, catalyst, transport, temperature and composition. A formal Arrhenius rate coefficient can summarize one mechanism over a limited temperature interval, but parameters are not universal constants of a named molecular formula. Some processes include reversible steps, intermediates, photochemical channels and competing phases. The NIST Chemical Kinetics Database contains measured and evaluated reaction-parameter records, so a future model must preserve the original reaction identity and bibliography alongside its numerical fit. A small offline simulation may verify differential-equation arithmetic while remaining empirically disconnected from any actual chemical pathway.

content.text: Electrochemistry underlies batteries, sensors, corrosion processes and some materials interfaces needed by computing hardware. Fick's first law is a constitutive approximation for one species in a medium under defined conditions; the coefficient D can depend strongly on temperature, composition, phase, defects and electric fields. Scientific continuity requires the governing equation, boundary conditions, grid resolution, time-step stability criterion, initial profile and a separate record of how D was measured.

content.text: A material's stable phase depends on temperature, pressure, composition and, sometimes, history.
